subject.title: Feature: enrich usage/status JSON with agent, cron, and channel labels

question: Should stable usage/status JSON grow first-class session attribution fields, and should `sessions.usage`, `status --json --usage`, or another usage surface own them with what privacy policy for channel targets?
rationale: Current main already exposes partial attribution, but the remaining work changes public JSON contracts and privacy semantics, so automation should not choose the API shape unilaterally.

options.title: Extend `sessions.usage` narrowly
options.body: Add optional stable low-cardinality attribution fields there first, document the contract, and omit raw channel target ids by default.

options.title: Fold attribution into status JSON
options.body: Make `status --json --usage` include or link per-session attribution, accepting a wider CLI status contract for automation consumers.

options.title: Defer to local dashboards
options.body: Keep current JSON surfaces as-is and leave cron/channel joins to local adapters until a broader telemetry design lands.

recommendation.title: Extend `sessions.usage` narrowly
recommendation.body: Add optional stable low-cardinality attribution fields there first, document the contract, and omit raw channel target ids by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is centered on the existing token usage dashboard and Gateway `sessions.usage` API history.
